whatTheyArgued: A doctrine (yan) is judged by three standards, all required: root (it rests on the deeds of the ancient sage-kings), source/verifiability (it is checked against what the common people have seen and heard), and use (adopting it in government benefits state and people). Mei 1929, Anti-Fatalism (I), verbatim snip.

scholarship.ref: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Mohism' (san biao: root, source, use)
scholarship.supports: three standards, their names, and that the middle one is what people see and hear
scholarship.disputes: Hansen (1985, 1992) reads them as pragmatic appropriateness of statements, not semantic truth; Graham (1989) and Harbsmeier (1998) dispute that

ourUse: grounding.js: a claim stands only if its numbers and names are string-contained in the cited material's bytes; Mozi is the namesake and the 'verifiability' test its justification.

bends.ours: Only the verifiability test is mechanized and presented as THE test ('a claim stands on what the eyes and ears can witness, or it does not stand').
bends.theirs: All three tests are required together; verifiability alone never settles a doctrine. Root and use are not implemented anywhere in grounding.js.

bends.ours: 'Witness' = literal string containment in a supplied document.
bends.theirs: The witnesses are the senses of hearing and sight of the common people: communal perception, not a text's bytes. Containment is our analogue, not Mozi's method.
The tests judge doctrines/statements about what ought to be done; whether they extend to plain factual truth is itself disputed (Hansen vs Graham).

bends.ours: archon-compendium.js describes the tests as 'eyes and ears, the ancients' experience, beneficial to the people' and reorders them, putting the senses first.
bends.theirs: Order in the source: basis, verifiability, applicability. The compendium also puts the quoted phrase 'It is in the bytes the eyes and ears can witness' in a work field read as the author's: that sentence is ours.

fix: compendium entry: restore three tests and order; mark the 'bytes' sentence ours
grounding.js header: say it mechanizes one of three, by analogy
